name: CodeReview
source: A practice project on multi-service web APIs by an outside developer, included in adapted form

upstream.name: code review pipeline (four FastAPI services and a sequential client)
upstream.author: an outside developer (practice project on multi-service web APIs)
upstream.license: no license file in the original repository
upstream.used_as: adapted copy: services in servers/code_review, client in workloads/code_review/review_client.py

extra_file.file: Lib/mailcap.py at CPython v3.9.16 (profiling split only)

unit: one Python source file (5 HTTP requests)

outputs.review_json: {action, review_text} of the /summarize response, JSON with sorted keys
outputs.lint_summary: lint counts and the first three diagnostics sent to /summarize
outputs.sec_summary: highest severity and all security issues sent to /summarize

equivalence: review_json identical (python -m wbench.compare --outputs review_json); action, lint_summary and sec_summary are expected identical as well
adaptations: Tracing removed: the services and the client no longer import the upstream profiling helper or write per-request trace records, and the services no longer print a log line per request.

Code paths the workflow does not use are removed: the parser's GET /ast/{id} endpoint and its in-memory AST store, the ast_id request field of /lint and /scan, the fields-based response trimming of /lint and /scan, the --parser-url option, and the summarizer's optional local-LLM backend.
The fields query parameter is still sent by the client, as in the original; the services return every field and ignore it.
ruff is started with --isolated so that configuration files above the service's working directory cannot change the rule set (on the 70 inputs the output is identical with and without the flag).

Scanner: the reference deployment ran a locally modified scanner (extra execution modes, not included) in the mode that runs the commit's code path, one Bandit process per request and no result cache, on a separate port; the released scanner is the commit's code on the upstream default port 8103.
Inputs come from a python.org tarball and one CPython git file instead of a local Python installation.

development_hardware.server: AMD EPYC 7763 node (the services are CPU only), RHEL 9.6, Python 3.10.22
development_hardware.client: Apple Mac, Python 3.10.18, reaching the services over an SSH tunnel (ping RTT about 30 ms)
development_hardware.original_author: Intel Core i9-13900F desktop, Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.10.12
